$comment: DECLARATIVE REGISTER OF IMMUTABLE ACTOR-ATTRIBUTION COLUMNS (GOV-H).
An actor column records WHO did something. That fact does not stop being true
when the actor's user row is deleted. So such a column must NOT carry a foreign
key into public.users: ON DELETE SET NULL erases the attribution, ON DELETE
CASCADE erases the evidence. Referential integrity is instead the WRITER's job —
it validates that the user exists at write time, which is the only moment the
claim is being made.
This file is CHECKED, not documentation. scripts/ci/check-actor-fk-compatibility.js
fails when the catalog and this register disagree in EITHER direction: a declared
column that does not exist, a declared-absent FK that is present, a declared
nullability that does not match, or an immutable actor column carrying a SET NULL
or CASCADE FK into public.users.
FIELDS
table, column        the column being governed (schema public).
immutable_actor      true  = attribution that must survive actor deletion.
false = ordinary ownership; an FK is fine. Recorded so the
advisory `undeclared_actor_fk` finding stays quiet
for a column that was considered and accepted.
fk_into_users        'absent'   = there must be NO FK into public.users.
'required' = an FK is expected (ownership columns only).
nullable             the column's required nullability. An immutable actor
column is nullable: a writer with no human actor (a system
action) legitimately leaves it unset, and a NOT NULL column
with no FK cannot express that.
check_constraint     the CHECK that binds the column, when one exists. The
detector reads the catalog for this; the name is recorded so
a rename is visible in review.
writer_validation    REQUIRED when fk_into_users is 'absent'. The module:symbol
that validates the referent exists before the write. Without
it, dropping the FK trades an erasure defect for a dangling
reference defect.
evidence             the evidence class behind the entry, in the programme's
vocabulary. PRODUCTION_CATALOG_VERIFIED entries were
observed in the 2026-11-01 production inventory.
status               'enforced'  = the schema is already in the required shape.
'remediating' = a track in flight owns the change; the
detector still reports, and the entry
records the intent, not a claim of fact.
OWNERSHIP: adding an entry here does NOT authorise a migration. The remediation
tracks (B, C, D, E) own their own migrations; this register is the control that
keeps the shape from regressing afterwards.
